questions.question: Which command lists the contents of `site.tar.gz` without extracting it?
questions.explanation: -t lists ("tell"), -z handles gzip and -f names the archive. -x extracts and -c creates.

questions.question: What is the difference between `rsync -a dist/ server:/var/www/shop/` and `rsync -a dist server:/var/www/shop/`?
options: The first deletes extra files on the server
The first is compressed in transit and the second is not
The first copies the contents of dist into shop/; the second creates shop/dist/
questions.explanation: A trailing slash on the source means "the contents of this directory". Without it, rsync copies the directory itself. A slash on the destination makes no difference.

questions.question: Why should you run `rsync` with `-n` before adding `--delete` to a real deployment?
options: -n is a dry run that shows what would be copied and deleted, so a wrong path cannot wipe files
-n makes rsync ask for confirmation for every file
questions.explanation: --delete removes destination files that are missing from the source. A dry run (-n / --dry-run) previews this so mistakes are caught before data is lost.

questions.question: Which is true about scp port options?
options: scp and ssh both use -p for the port
scp has no way to use a non-standard port
scp uses capital -P for the port, while ssh uses lowercase -p
scp reads the port only from the URL, like scp host:2222/path
questions.explanation: In scp, lowercase -p preserves timestamps and modes, so the port flag is capital -P. ssh uses lowercase -p for the port.
